question: How much should I spend testing whether the skill works?

options.label: Reviewer check, then A/B (Recommended)
options.description: Now: one call to the installed roblox-ui-reviewer on the round-2 renders, about 75–85k tokens like the dry run's reviews. After the fixes: two new briefs, each built by an Opus agent with the skill and by one without, plus about 6 reviewer calls. You then judge the renders without knowing which is which. The build runs' cost hasn't been measured.

options.label: Reviewer check only
options.description: One call. Shows that the shipped reviewer works, but not whether the skill beats an agent without it.

options.label: Neither for now
options.description: The first real game screen becomes the test.

question: Should I open a skill PR for the gaps I confirmed?

options.label: Yes, open it (Recommended)
options.description: A colour sampler for reference images, a rule for users with no references, `uv run` for every script, no Ship while one of the brief's top-ranked items isn't drawn, a note that the guard checks Luau only, and the dry-run project raised to the current text sizes. You merge it, as with the pins.

options.label: Not now
options.description: The gaps stay: agents will guess reference colours, and may stall when a user has no references.

question: The skill steers agents toward restrained UI. Which default suits players aged 10 to 16?

options.label: Bold to calm tiles (Recommended)
options.description: Keep the AI-tells list, but scope it by audience, and make one of the three style tiles bold: saturated, chunky, outlined text. You still pick the direction.

options.label: Keep restraint
options.description: Agents keep steering to calm, flat UI unless the brief asks otherwise.

options.label: Lean bold
options.description: Make bold, saturated game UI the default, and loosen the tells.
